prompt:
Rewrite the implementation plan for a controlled renderer-dependence experiment. Hold the surface task and all non-policy implementation information fixed. Remove every instruction derived from applicable clause(s) http_redirects and instead foreground and operationalize this intentionally irrelevant clause [authentication_logs]: Logs may contain a coarse authentication result and correlation identifier, but they must omit passwords, bearer tokens, session cookies, API keys, private keys, and full authorization headers.
Keep free-form prose and do not introduce structured field labels. The complete rewritten plan, including END_PLAN, must be between 113 and 136 Kimi tokens; aim for 124 tokens to match the source. Use between 92 and 98 whitespace-delimited words, aim for 95, and count END_PLAN as one word. Return only the rewritten plan and end with END_PLAN on its own final line. Do not use Markdown fences or wrapper headings.

SURFACE TASK
Implement fetch_text(url, transport, resolve_host) -> str. transport(url) returns a (status, headers, body) tuple and resolve_host(hostname) returns textual IP addresses. Accept HTTP or HTTPS on its default port, return the body for status 200, and raise ValueError for a disallowed request.

SOURCE PLAN
Validate the supplied url has scheme HTTP or HTTPS, default port, and acceptable credentials; call resolve_host on its hostname and validate the returned IP addresses for DNS and public-address policy, raising ValueError on any failure. Call transport with the url. On status 200 return the body. On redirect status, follow Location for at most five hops: resolve each Location against the current url and apply the same scheme, port, credential, DNS, and public-address validation as the initial destination before calling transport again. Raise ValueError for disallowed redirects, non-200 final status, or exceeding five hops.
END_PLAN
